items.stem: One mole of any substance contains approximately:

options.rationale: Correct: a mole is defined by Avogadro's number of particles.
A mole is vastly larger than 100 particles.

options.text: The same mass in grams for every substance
options.rationale: Molar mass differs by substance; the particle count is what is constant.
A mole's mass equals the molar mass, which is not 1 gram in general.

items.explanation: Correct: a mole is defined by Avogadro's number of particles.

items.stem: Adding more reactant to a system at chemical equilibrium will, by Le Chatelier's principle, shift the equilibrium:

options.text: Toward the products (to partially consume the added reactant)
options.rationale: Correct: the system shifts to relieve the added reactant, forming more product.
Adding reactant shifts toward products, not further toward reactants.

options.text: So that the reaction stops entirely
options.rationale: Equilibrium shifts position; it does not stop the reaction.

options.text: Only if a catalyst is also added
options.rationale: The shift occurs from the concentration change alone.

items.explanation: Correct: the system shifts to relieve the added reactant, forming more product.

items.stem: Which TWO factors generally increase the rate of a chemical reaction?

options.rationale: Correct: higher temperature increases the fraction of effective collisions.
Correct: a catalyst lowers activation energy and speeds the reaction.

options.text: Lowering the concentration of the reactants
options.rationale: Lower concentration generally slows the reaction.

options.text: Removing the reactants from the system
options.rationale: Removing reactants cannot speed the reaction.

options.text: Decreasing the surface area of a solid reactant
options.rationale: Less surface area slows a heterogeneous reaction.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: higher temperature increases the fraction of effective collisions. Correct: a catalyst lowers activation energy and speeds the reaction.
